div.note: Liebermann prints H (Textus Roffensis f. 94v, after Norðleod, c. 1120) and B (Cambridge, Corpus Christi College 383, p. 84, after A Gu, c. 1125). K is B; H is also given here. Both headings are in red; B's is not original. Liebermann calls this a private work, favourable to the bride's side; the archetype of H and B already shows forms of c. 1075, the original already has Norse loanwords; what Edgar's reform and Cnut still demanded holds here (8 f.). He dates it c. 970 (1030?)–c. 1060. In B ‘aghon’ the ‘a’ is illegible through a stain. Italics removed from the clause number for consistency.; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “c.970 (1030?) –c.1060; 1008–1020 (Wormald); no clear indication of date; probably not early (Whitelock)”, now “c.970 (1030?)–c.1060 (Liebermann); no clear indication of date; probably not early (Whitelock); 1008–1020 (Wormald)”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “c.970 (1030?)–c.1060 (Liebermann); no clear indication of date; probably not early (Whitelock); 1008–1020 (Wormald)”, now “c.970 (1030?)–c.1060 (Liebermann, I p. 442); no clear indication of date; probably not early (Whitelock, EHD p. 474); 1008–1020 (Wormald, MEL p. 386)”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “H 442; B 442; Q 443; German 443”; 10 rows of Wif)

note.seg: Die Überschrift in H scheint zwar der in Q verwandt. Allein letztere eignet nur der jüngsten Rezension, die Rubriken aus dem Lateinischen Text zu erfinden pflegt. Die älteren Q-Formen tragen keine Überschrift.—Die Überschrift in H, die ein bei Toller nur hierher belegtes Wort bringt, kann des Schreibers H Eigentum sein

The heading in H does seem related to that in Q. But the latter belongs only to the youngest recension, which is in the habit of inventing rubrics from the Latin text. The older Q forms bear no heading. — The heading in H, which contains a word attested in Toller only here, may be the scribe H’s own work
Nicht ‘Wettvertrag’ (Sohm Recht d. Eheschliess. 315), auch nicht ‘Heirat’
Not ‘wager contract’ (Sohm Recht d. Eheschliess. 315), nor ‘marriage’ either

In B gehört der zweite Teil der Überschrift dem 12. Jh; dagegen die ersten fünf Wörter sind vermutlich vom selben Rechtskompilator hbq wie die Überschriften zu Swerian und Wer (s. o. S. 231. 234), zwischen welchen Stücken Wif in Q steht

In B the second part of the heading belongs to the 12th cent.; the first five words, on the other hand, are presumably by the same legal compiler hbq as the headings to Swerian and Wer (see above p. 231. 234), between which pieces Wif stands in Q
Der Fall der Witwe (c. 1) fehlt; die Überschrift ist also nicht original. Doch vergisst auch Verf. 2. 8 diesen Fall
The case of the widow (c. 1) is missing; the heading is therefore not original. But the author too forgets this case in 2. 8

forewearda in Ann. Agsax. 1109; so heissen Eheverträge um 1018 Earle 228; Thorpe 320. Die Endung -e ist Mittelenglisch. Ebenso das h in aghon. Vgl. über die einzelnen Verabredungen Gl Eheschliessung 4a

forewearda in Ann. Agsax. 1109; marriage contracts are so called c. 1018, Earle 228; Thorpe 320. The ending -e is Middle English. So too the h in aghon. On the individual agreements cf. Gl Eheschliessung 4a

As family law and inheritance are subjects on which we are badly informed, this short text, which survives in the Textus Roffensis and the C.C.C.C., MS. 383, and in Latin in Quadripartitus, is welcome. It bears no clear indication of date. Liebermann would place it 975–1030, with a preference for the latter part of this period. The stressing of the need that the woman herself is to accept the suitor suggests that it is not early, and so does the use of the Norse word sammæle. It is edited by Liebermann, I, 442–4, and with English translation by Thorpe, I, 254–7. [Her footnote 5: No. 51 in the 1955 edition]
